group_assessment.weighting: Neonatal Sprague-Dawley rat pups (75 randomised, three groups), repeated insulin hypoglycaemia on P2, P4, P6, 2 h daily visual stimulation P14-P28, MRI on a subset, PTZ seizure score at P28, immunohistochemistry for BDNF and synaptophysin. The paper is about visual stimulation, not about glucose therapy; its hypoglycaemia arm is a model of injury. Reported numbers are internally inconsistent in several places (n, t statistics, glucose threshold, one SYN value), so the group differences are weak evidence even in this model. Not a WWOX system.

entries.proposition: Hypoglycaemia was induced with insulin 40 U/kg i.p. on postnatal days 2, 4 and 6 in rat pups.
entries.snippet: Rats in the NH and NH-V groups were intraperitoneally injected with insulin (40 U/kg, 10 mL/400 U, Jiangsu Wanbang) on postnatal days 2, 4, and 6 to induce hypoglycemia.

entries.proposition: Hypoglycaemia was terminated with an intraperitoneal 50% glucose bolus of 2 mL/kg after the fifth glucose reading (about 4 h).
entries.snippet: After the 5th blood glucose measurement, a 2 mL/kg intraperitoneal injection of 50% glucose was administered to terminate hypoglycemia, and the rats were returned to their mothers.

entries.proposition: Pups with spontaneous seizures or death during modelling were excluded, a selection step that removes the most severely affected animals.
entries.snippet: Rats that experienced spontaneous seizures or death during the model development process were excluded from the study.

entries.proposition: The text says the 3 h and 4 h glucose values were below the meter threshold of 0.06 mmol/L, while Table 1 lists 4 h values as 0.6-0.8 mmol/L or lower; the inclusion rule was 0.8 mmol/L or lower.
entries.snippet: Data from 3 and 4 h after insulin injection were below the measurement threshold (<0.06 mmol/L).

entries.proposition: Table 1 lists the 4 h values as at most 0.6, 0.6 and 0.8 mmol/L on days 2, 4 and 6 (not the text's below 0.06).
Only 10 of 25 pups per group were imaged, and 5 of the 10 NH pups showed an abnormal occipital signal.
entries.snippet: In the NH group, 5 rats exhibited structural damage of varying severity, characterized by mixed signals in the occipital region, predominantly low signals (Figure 1B).

entries.proposition: Figure 1 shows one axial T2 slice per group, with a single arrow in group B at the dorsal midline region; one slice does not establish occipital location or lesion extent, and the control and model slices differ in window settings.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 1: panels A (control) and B (model) are single axial FSE T2-weighted slices at 4.7 T; panel B carries one white arrow near the dorsal midline; the on-image windowing values differ between panels (WL 2048/WW 4095 versus WL 1495/WW 2989).

experimental_context.system: Sprague-Dawley rat at about P21, 4.7 T MRI

entries.proposition: Seizure scores after PTZ were 2.4 control, 4.1 model, 3.0 visual-stimulation, with n = 25 stated per group.

The reported t statistics (-3.431 and -2.283) do not match n = 25 per group with the tabulated means and SDs: they correspond to roughly 5-6 (N versus NH) and 8-9 (NH-V versus NH) animals per group, while a t test on the tabulated values with n = 25 gives about 7 for N versus NH (reader's arithmetic, not stated in the paper).
entries.snippet: the N group had significantly lower seizure scores compared to the NH group (t = −3.431, p = 0.008)

contradicts_locator.what_changed: animals-per-group estimate corrected from about 10 to about 5-9

entries.proposition: The synaptophysin table gives 0.235 in the visual-stimulation group against 0.024 and 0.021 in the other groups, a tenfold step inconsistent with the BDNF column and the text; likely a decimal slip, not resolvable from the paper.
The Discussion calls the MRI finding 'inconsistent' with earlier work in one sentence and 'consistent' in another.
entries.snippet: Head MRI scans showed low signals in the occipital lobe of NH group rats, indicating occipital lobe damage, which is inconsistent with previous studies on hypoglycemic brain injury (3, 4).

entries.proposition: The authors report that the result differed from their own initial hypothesis that stimulation would increase susceptibility.
entries.snippet: indicating that visual stimulation reduced the epileptic susceptibility of HBIN rats, which was different from our initial hypothesis.

entries.proposition: The authors name immature inhibitory synapses at the age of testing and state that further research is needed.
entries.snippet: The animals used in this experiment were 2-day-old rats, where inhibitory synapses had not yet matured.

entries.proposition: The animal work used a very severe, repeated, insulin-induced hypoglycaemia (glucose at or below about 0.6-0.8 mmol/L for hours) in 2-day-old pups.
entries.snippet: Rats in the NH and NH-V groups were included in the study if their blood glucose levels reached ≤0.8 mmol/L 4 h after insulin injection
